categories.tagline: How XivMcp reaches past the running game: the title screen, the sibling mods and other plugins.

ideas.title: Approvals That Wait for the Pull to End
ideas.pitch: An agent's gated call that arrives mid-fight becomes a ticket instead of a prompt, and the prompt appears once you are out of combat.
ideas.experience: You are in the middle of a trash pull when Claude Code decides your macro needs rewriting. Nothing pops up over your hotbars. When the last mob drops, a quiet toast says 'Claude Code is waiting: write macro 12' and the Approvals tab carries a (1).
ideas.how: ConfirmationService.ApproveToolCallAsync reads ICondition first: while InCombat (or BoundByDuty with the duty started, the flags get_conditions and get_duty_state already read) it does not open ConfirmWindow but files the call through the same path request_action uses into ApprovalQueue/TicketStore, and the tools/call answers with the ticket id so the client can follow the resume contract in APPROVALS.md. ApprovalWiring's 1 Hz tick raises the toast when the condition clears. A setting under Advanced in MainWindow.Settings.cs turns it off.
ideas.risks: Clients that do not implement the ticket resume contract see a call that never completes, so the answer must say plainly what happened. The 20-second prompt timeout and the call timeout both need rethinking for this path. Condition flags are among the ClientStructs members not yet observed in game. With approval switched off it changes nothing, which is correct but should be said in the setting's text.
ideas.audience: anyone who plays with an agent connected, raiders and roulette runners especially

ideas.title: Show Me the Before and After
ideas.pitch: The approval prompt for write_macro, equip_gearset and set_plugin_enabled shows what is there now next to what will be there, not only a sentence.
ideas.experience: Codex asks to rewrite macro 7. The prompt shows your old six lines on the left, its new ones on the right, with the changed lines tinted. For a gear set you see each slot's item level before and after, and one red row where the new set drops your ring.
ideas.how: Tools that already carry an approval sentence gain an optional preview callback: MacroWriteProvider reads the slot through MacroMemory, GearsetProvider reads the target set and get_equipment's current slots. The preview is rendered by ConfirmWindow and the Approvals tab (MainWindow.Approvals.cs) as a two-column table. It also lets McpServer.RenderApprovalSummary stop truncating write_macro at 500 characters, the open point in TODO.md. ToolContractTests gains a check that a preview never replaces the sentence.
ideas.risks: The preview is taken when the prompt opens; the macro could change before approval, so the write must compare against the preview and fail if it moved. Reading macro and gear set memory needs the framework thread before the window draws. A long diff makes the prompt tall.
ideas.audience: cautious players, macro hoarders, anyone letting an agent tidy their setup

ideas.title: The Receipt at Session's End
ideas.pitch: When an agent disconnects, a quest-complete toast and a one-page receipt of everything it read, changed, was denied and failed at.
ideas.experience: You come back from making tea. Almanac's session has closed and the quest-complete fanfare plays: 'Almanac finished: 41 reads, 2 changes, 1 denied'. Opening the receipt shows the teleport it asked for, the macro it wrote, and the chat line you refused.
ideas.how: Sessions.cs already knows when a session's lifetime ends (IsClosed, StreamClosed). ServerHost counts ActivityRecorded per session; on close it builds a summary from those counts and the matching ActionLog entries, shows it with IToastGui.ShowQuest as ObjectiveTracker does, and keeps the last twenty receipts in the Activity tab (MainWindow.Activity.cs). With approval off the receipt lists every change, since those ran without a prompt.
ideas.risks: Streamable HTTP sessions often end by expiry rather than a clean close, so some receipts arrive minutes late. Clients that open a new session per call would produce a toast storm; receipts need a minimum size and a mute. Tool arguments in the receipt may hold chat text, so it stays local.
ideas.audience: players who leave agents running, owners who run with approval off

ideas.title: Keys That Open Only Some Doors
ideas.pitch: Each per-client token carries its own list of categories, so the benchmark client can read game data but never your chat or your bags.
ideas.experience: In Settings you issue a token for a friend's model experiment and untick chat, inventory and party. Their client lists sixty tools instead of a hundred and fifty, and a call to read_chat answers that the tool does not exist for this key.
ideas.how: ClientTokenEntry (AutoApprovePolicy.cs) gains an optional category allow-list, edited in MainWindow.Policy.cs and settable through XivMcp.ConnectClient. The request scope already knows which token authenticated; tools/list, resources/list and dispatch filter by it after HostState's global tiers and categories, so a scope can only narrow. Changing a token's scope sends list_changed to that client's sessions only.
ideas.risks: Core/Abstractions and McpServer's public surface are frozen, so this must be an additive hook. Clients without a per-client token share the global view, which the UI must make obvious. Resources and templates cut across categories (ffxiv://chat/recent) and need their own mapping. It is a boundary between clients, not a sandbox for a hostile one.
ideas.audience: players who connect more than one client, tailnet users, anyone testing a new model

ideas.title: An Agent May Ask You One Question
ideas.pitch: A Ui tool that puts a short multiple-choice question on your screen and hands the answer back, so an agent stops guessing which gear set or which retainer you meant.
ideas.experience: Planning your crafting run, the agent is unsure. A small window in the game's style asks: 'Sell the extra Darksteel Ore, or keep it for the Grade 4 materia recipe?' with two buttons and 'Not now'. You click Keep and the plan updates in your terminal.
ideas.how: A new ask_player tool (Ui tier, marked RequiresApproval=false as it only displays to the owner, listed in ToolContractTests' display-only set) takes a question and two to five choices, returns a question id at once and exposes ffxiv://questions/{id} with notifications/resources/updated on the answer, the same shape as tickets. The window reuses ConfirmWindow's layout and the pull-safe hold for combat. MCP's own elicitation/create is a later option once clients render it; McpServer.Dispatch has no handler for it today.
ideas.risks: A chatty agent could ask twenty questions an hour; it needs a per-client cap and a 'stop asking' button. Answers are free text to the model, so choices must stay short labels, never a way to route the player into a gated action without its own prompt. Clients that do not subscribe to resources must poll.
ideas.audience: players using agents for planning, Almanac users

ideas.title: Agent Progress as Tracked Quests
ideas.pitch: The agent board's running entries appear under the Duty List next to custom objectives, with a progress line and a quest toast when one finishes.
ideas.experience: Below 'The Porcelain Prisoner' in your Duty List sits 'Claude Code: refactoring loader, 3/7, 42 %'. You finish a FATE; the line turns to 'Done' and the quest-complete chime plays. A failed one turns red and stays until you hover and dismiss it.
ideas.how: ObjectiveOverlay already draws native-styled rows under DutyListAnchor. A second section reads AgentBoard (subscribing to its change event as the IPC Changed gate does) and draws each running post as title plus status line, with the Progress value as a thin bar in the Duty List's colours. Done and Failed transitions call IToastGui.ShowQuest as ObjectiveTracker does. A Settings toggle beside 'Custom objectives' chooses board, objectives or both.
ideas.risks: The overlay itself has never been seen in game (OBJECTIVES.md checklist), so this inherits every placement question. Five busy agents crowd the Duty List; it needs a cap and collapse. Agent names and status text are client-supplied and must be length-capped and cleaned before drawing.
ideas.audience: developers running agents while they play, Ghostty and Almanac users

ideas.title: Pending Approvals Where You Already Look
ideas.pitch: Open approval tickets show as a single tracked line under the Duty List, so a request filed while you were away is noticed without opening the plugin window.
ideas.experience: You log back in after dinner. Under your quests: '2 requests waiting: teleport to Kugane (Codex), write macro 3 (Claude Code)'. Clicking it opens the Approvals tab on the first one; nothing is approved from the overlay itself.
ideas.how: APPROVALS.md names the hook: ApprovalQueue.Changed and Snapshot(). ObjectiveOverlay reads the pending count and the first two summaries (the existing approval sentences) and draws one entry; its click calls the same toggle as the XivMcp.ToggleWindow IPC gate with the Approvals tab selected.
ideas.risks: Approving from a Duty List row would be one mis-click from an unintended teleport, so the row only opens the tab, and that has to stay true. Ticket reasons are client text and are shown only in the tab, not the overlay. Same unverified overlay placement as objectives.
ideas.audience: players who file tickets from agents while away, anyone using the ticket queue

ideas.title: A Linkshell for Your Agents
ideas.pitch: A private in-game channel where agents post short messages in their own colour and you reply with a slash command, delivered to them as a resource update.
ideas.experience: Your chat log shows '[MCP:claude] Tests pass. Want me to open the PR?' in pale gold. You type '/xivmcp say claude yes, draft only' without leaving the game, and a minute later the reply comes back that the draft is up. Nobody else sees a word of it.
ideas.how: print_echo already writes [MCP]-tagged lines to the player's own log only. Give each client a stable colour and prefix, and add `/xivmcp say <agent> <text>` in the command handler Plugin.cs registers; messages go to a bounded per-client inbox exposed as ffxiv://inbox with notifications/resources/updated through NotifierProxy, plus a read_inbox tool. The EventStream gains a 'message' kind so get_events clients see it too.
ideas.risks: Echo lines are the player's own log, but they still sit in chat logs that other plugins read and export, so secrets posted by an agent end up there. Clients must subscribe to resources for replies to feel live. A /say typo such as '/say claude' would post in public Say chat, so the command name must be hard to confuse.
ideas.audience: developers who play between agent turns, Ghostty users away from their terminal

ideas.title: Pin This Spot as an Objective
ideas.pitch: `/xivmcp quests here "Title"` records your zone, map coordinates, the current bell and weather as a new objective, and `export` writes the lot as a pack to share.
ideas.experience: You find the perfect screenshot spot above Costa del Sol at dusk in clear skies. One command and it is on your Duty List with the flag, the window 'ET 18:00-20:00, Clear Skies' and a 30-yalm radius. Exported, it loads straight into a friend's game.
ideas.how: ObjectiveCommands.cs gains 'here' and 'export' next to its ten verbs. 'here' reads the territory and player position as get_location does, converts to map x/y with the same maths as CoordinateProvider and set_map_flag, reads the live weather from WeatherManager and the Eorzea bell from the clock EorzeaTimeWindow uses, then builds the objective through ObjectiveFactory. 'export' serialises the store in the ObjectivePack format that load_objective_pack reads.
ideas.risks: What time window to record is a guess: the current bell alone is too narrow, so it defaults to no time condition and says so. Weather in fixed-weather zones is reported as a problem by the evaluator, which is correct but surprising. Export paths under Wine need the same Z: mapping as load.
ideas.audience: screenshot takers, gposers, pack authors, friends sharing sightseeing routes

ideas.title: Real Rows in the Duty List
ideas.pitch: Replace the overlay with native nodes inside the Duty List itself, so custom objectives and agent posts move, collapse and hide exactly as quests do.
ideas.experience: Your custom objectives sit in the Duty List under a 'Custom' header, and when you accept a quest the list reflows with them in it. HUD scale, alignment and the collapse arrow all behave as the game's own rows do, because they are the game's own rows.
ideas.how: Option (a) in OBJECTIVES.md: node injection into _ToDoList through IAddonLifecycle (PostSetup, PostRequestedUpdate, PostRefresh, PreFinalize), either through KamiToolKit or Dalamud's native overlay service once goatcorp/Dalamud#2874 is merged. It is a drop-in for ObjectiveOverlay and DutyListAnchor; ObjectiveStore, the evaluator and the tools do not change.
ideas.risks: AddonToDoList has no slot for plugin rows and rebuilds its ListPanel itself; a node still linked at finalize (zone change, HUD layout change, unload) crashes the game rather than failing softly. KamiToolKit is a large dependency to keep current with patches. None of it can be tested outside the running game.
ideas.audience: players who want XivMcp to feel like part of the game

ideas.title: Your Unfinished Sightseeing Log, as Objectives
ideas.pitch: A tool that reads which vistas you have not logged and posts each as a custom objective with its spot, emote, Eorzea time and weather window.
ideas.experience: You ask Almanac what is left in your Stormblood log. Six entries appear under your Duty List, two of them 'Ready now (14 min left)'. Clicking the first flags the vista on the map; the step reads 'Go to the spot, then /lookout'.
ideas.how: A static provider reads the Adventure sheet through IGameDataSource (so the standalone host can answer the data half) for the Level location, emote and time columns; a live half checks completion through ClientStructs' PlayerState adventure flags via ILiveWorld. The result feeds ObjectiveFactory directly, and the time and weather become the objective's eorzeaTime and weather conditions that ObjectiveEvaluator and find_weather_windows already compute.
ideas.risks: Which Adventure columns carry the weather requirement must be checked against Lumina and may need a small hand-kept table for some entries. The completion flags are unverified in game like every ClientStructs read here. Posting a whole expansion's log at once hits the 200-objective cap, so it works a region at a time.

ideas.title: The Weekly Ledger
ideas.pitch: One live resource that says what the daily and weekly resets have left for you: roulettes, tomestone cap headroom, and the reset times in your local time.
ideas.experience: Tuesday evening, the agent board shows 'Weekly: 180 tomestones to cap, Expert roulette not done, resets in 3 h'. You finish the roulette, and the line updates when the bonus is spent.
ideas.how: A ffxiv://reset resource combines what already exists: get_roulette_status, the tomestone weekly figures from get_currencies and the reset schedule from get_time, with resources/updated on the 'duty' and 'inventory' events EventStream already appends. The plan_daily_reset prompt switches to reading it. Optionally it posts itself as a single objective with a note line.
ideas.risks: Much of what players count as weekly (Wondrous Tails, custom deliveries, Doman enclave) lives in managers whose ClientStructs fields are unverified and may not be loaded until the relevant window has been opened. It must show 'unknown' rather than 'done' for those. Reset times shift with daylight saving in the player's zone.
ideas.audience: players on a weekly routine, returners who forget what resets when

ideas.title: Dresser and Armoire Tidy
ideas.pitch: A read-only report of glamour items that could move to the Armoire, duplicates across dresser and bags, and sets that could be combined into outfits.
ideas.experience: Your dresser is full again. The agent answers with three lists: 22 items that belong in the Armoire, 5 you own twice, and 3 sets one piece short of becoming an outfit, with where the missing piece sits (retainer 2). You do the moving yourself.
ideas.how: A new tool in the Inventory providers joins the dresser contents GlamourProvider already reads with InventoryReader's containers and cached retainer inventories, then checks each item against the Cabinet sheet (Armoire-eligible) and the MirageStoreSetItem sheet (outfit sets) through IGameDataSource. It returns lists only; nothing is moved.
ideas.risks: Dresser and retainer contents are only loaded after the player has opened them this session, so the answer must say which containers were not seen. Outfit rules around dyes and duplicates have edge cases. Pure planning, which is the point, but some will ask it to do the moving; it must not.
ideas.audience: glamour collectors, anyone whose dresser is always full

ideas.title: Next Three Upgrades
ideas.pitch: For your current job, the three cheapest item-level gains you can reach, what each costs in tomestones, seals or crafted materials, and what you already hold towards it.
ideas.experience: Fresh to 100 on Dancer, you ask what to do first. The answer: the tomestone earrings (you have 375 of 375), the crafted body (the ingredient tree is two steps from what you own), and the Normal raid bracelet, with the shop NPC flagged on your map.
ideas.how: A plan_gear_upgrades tool (GameData, with a live half) takes get_equipment's slots, searches equippable items above each slot's level with the same index search_items uses, ranks by item level gain per unit cost from ItemSources (SpecialShop and GilShop rows) and RecipeTree, and compares against get_currencies and find_owned_items. The gear_audit prompt calls it.
ideas.risks: Real best-in-slot depends on stat tiers and substat weights the game data does not state; this ranks by item level and cost only, and must say so. SpecialShop parsing is the messiest data in the sheets. Raid drops are not in the sheets at all.
ideas.audience: levelling players, alt-job owners, returning players gearing up

ideas.title: What Is This Craft Worth
ideas.pitch: Cost to craft from the full recipe tree against recent sale prices on your data centre, with the age of every price shown.
ideas.experience: You wonder whether the new housing item is worth crafting. The agent lays out the tree: ingredients you own at zero, the rest priced from recent sales, total 38,000 gil against a median sale of 61,000 two hours ago. You go gather the ore yourself.
ideas.how: Combine get_recipe_tree (RecipeTree), find_owned_items and get_market_prices (UniversalisClient behind MarketCache) into one tool or prompt: price leaves by median recent sale, mark owned quantities as free, and report the age of each price. The crafting_plan prompt gains a 'with prices' variant.
ideas.risks: Universalis data is crowd-sourced and can be hours stale; a thin market gives misleading medians. A deep tree asks for many items and must batch within the 20-item call and be polite with the cache. It stays on reading public prices and never touches the market board UI, per HARD-LINES.md; alerts on single listings are deliberately left out.
ideas.audience: crafters, gil-makers who do their own crafting, FC workshop planners

ideas.title: Last Known State Before Login
ideas.pitch: The pre-game standalone host answers character questions from a snapshot the plugin saved at logout, clearly labelled with its age.
ideas.experience: At work, over the tailnet, you ask what is in your saddlebag. Instead of 'game not running' the answer comes back with 'as of yesterday 23:14, when you logged out'. Log in and the plugin takes the port and answers live again.
ideas.how: On the 'session' logout event the plugin writes a snapshot of a small allow-listed set of read tools (get_player, get_inventory, get_currencies, get_job_levels, list_gearsets) to a file next to objectives.json. LiveToolStubs in the standalone host serves those tools from the snapshot with an asOf field instead of game_not_running, and everything else keeps its stub. HandoffCoordinator is unchanged.
ideas.risks: It puts inventory and character data in a file on disk that a tailnet client can reach, so it is off by default and never includes chat or party. Stale answers presented as live would mislead agents; asOf must be in every result and in the description. The standalone host has only been run between native processes.
ideas.audience: players who plan away from the PC, tailnet users, standalone host users

ideas.title: Other Plugins Can Offer Tools
ideas.pitch: An IPC gate through which any Dalamud plugin registers its own read tools with XivMcp, under the same catalogue, rate limit and approval gate.
ideas.experience: Your favourite housing plugin adds three read tools in its next update. In XivMcp's Tools tab they appear under 'from HousingPlugin', and your agent can ask it for the saved layout of your apartment.
ideas.how: Core already describes tools by data through ExternalTool (McpServer.Extensions.cs), which the standalone host uses. A new IpcContract gate lets a plugin register ExternalTool descriptions whose handler calls back into that plugin's own IPC. They sit under a per-plugin category the player enables in Settings, and anything not Read goes through ConfirmationService like every other gated tool.
ideas.risks: XivMcp cannot see what another plugin's handler does, so HARD-LINES.md cannot be enforced on it; the first version should allow Read tier only, and say so. ToolContractTests cannot check runtime tools. A plugin that unloads leaves dead tools until list_changed. IpcContract is a frozen, additive-only contract.
ideas.audience: Dalamud plugin authors, players who run several plugins with agents

ideas.title: Per-Client Call Meter
ideas.pitch: The Status tab shows each connected client's calls per minute against the rate limit, and the long-missing rate-limit control lands under Advanced.
ideas.experience: The game hitches and you open XivMcp. One bar is nearly full: a script polling get_events four times a second. You lower the limit from 600 to 120 and watch it settle.
ideas.how: TODO.md lists it: RateLimitPerMinute exists with no UI; add the input under Advanced in MainWindow.Settings.cs. The per-client bucket McpServer already keeps for RateLimitPerMinute and RateLimitBurst exposes its current fill, read by MainWindow.Status.cs as one bar per client, and get_server_info gains the same numbers.
ideas.risks: Client names are self-reported unless a per-client token is used, so two clients can share a bar. Reading the buckets from the draw loop must not take the same lock the dispatch path holds.
ideas.audience: players running several clients, anyone debugging a greedy agent

ideas.title: Terminal Layouts That Remember the House
ideas.pitch: Saved Ghostty layouts tied to a housing plot and room, so apply_terminal_layout puts your panels back on the same wall every time you walk in.
ideas.experience: You enter your apartment and ask the agent to set up for work. Three terminals appear exactly where you left them last night, one over the desk and two beside the window. Walk out and they fold back to pets.
ideas.how: get_terminal_layouts and apply_terminal_layout already exist and answer 'unavailable', because TODO.md notes that '/term pin' has no absolute world-position form. This needs that form in GhosttyDalamud first, then layouts keyed by get_housing_info's ward, plot and room, written through the layout.get/layout.set verbs that SiblingIpcProposals.cs leaves out today.
ideas.risks: The blocking work is in another mod and has to be designed there. Housing interiors share coordinates across plots, so the key must include the house identity. The sibling IPC patches have not been applied or built. Panels have no depth test and show through walls.
ideas.audience: Ghostty users who work from their house, FC workshop builders
